description:
## Why

PKIX-xj81 decomposition (shared infra). The 6 stress-pattern fixture beads
(PKIX-xj81.B through .G) all need a common openssl-driven generator and a
common Rust-side loader. Building that once here keeps each topology bead
small and independent.

## What

1. Create `pkix-path-builder/tests/fixtures/` directory.
2. Write `pkix-path-builder/tests/fixtures/generate.sh`:
   - Requires nothing but openssl 3.x + bash.
   - Creates a synthetic root CA (`StressRoot`) with a stable serial and a
     known SKI.
   - Defines reusable shell functions to issue intermediates and end-entity
     certs with explicit AKI/SKI/SPKI parameters (so per-topology beads can
     call `issue_intermediate $issuer_key $subject_name $aki_value` etc.).
   - Generates a small set of "always-present" fixtures shared across all
     topology beads (the root cert; possibly a per-test EE template).
   - Emits DER files only. PEM intermediate files used during generation
     are removed at the end so the only committed artifacts are DER.
   - Idempotent: re-running with the same RNG seed (`-rand seed-file`) is
     deterministic so fixtures do not churn between regenerations.
3. Write a small Rust helper module `pkix-path-builder/tests/common/mod.rs`
   exposing:
   - `fn stress_cert(name: &str) -> Certificate` mirroring `pkits_cert` but
     pointing at the new fixtures directory.
   - `fn stress_trust_anchor() -> TrustAnchor` returning the synthetic root.
   - `const STRESS_NOW: u64` — a unix timestamp safely inside the synthetic
     cert validity window. The generator must set validity windows that
     contain this constant.
4. Commit the generated `StressRoot.crt` DER file under
   `pkix-path-builder/tests/fixtures/` plus the generator script.
5. Document provenance in the module-level doc of `common/mod.rs`:
   openssl version used, command line invoked, date generated.

## Acceptance

- [ ] `bash pkix-path-builder/tests/fixtures/generate.sh` produces the same
      DER bytes as committed when re-run on the same machine with the same
      seed file.
- [ ] The Rust helper module compiles and exposes the three items above.
- [ ] `cargo test -p pkix-path-builder` passes (no existing tests should
      change behaviour; the new helper is only consumed by future beads).
- [ ] No new runtime deps; `std` is fine (this is test code).

## Out of scope

- The per-topology fixture trees themselves. Those are PKIX-xj81.B
  through .G.
title: pkix-path-builder: shared cert-generation infra for stress-pattern fixtures
